research: The archival abstract lists Anna, wife of Johann Amman von Rosenberg, among many people healed in Nuremberg. The wording can denote Johann Amman from a place called Rosenberg; it does not establish that he was a noble Hans von Rosenberg or identify which Rosenberg place. Franken, Sulzbach and Vestenberg associations are therefore not distinguishable from this evidence; the generated Hans/Amtmann mention is not independent evidence. See the archive catalogue: https://www.gda.bayern.de/gvl/document/e5589497-47d3-4fea-9778-f4ce15fe7549. Attribution unresolved. The Latin original reads “Anna Johannis Amans uxor de Rosenperg Eysten. dioc.” It identifies Anna as Johann Aman’s wife and places her at Rosenberg in the Diocese of Eichstätt, a detail omitted from the abstract. The catalogue separately indexes both spouses under Amman (Aman). This supports reading Rosenberg as a place of residence. The locality and any link to a listed house remain unverified. https://www.gda.bayern.de/digitalisat/iiif/e5589497-47d3-4fea-9778-f4ce15fe7549/1/340,3290,2800,220/max/0/default.jpg

entries.summary: Notariatsinstrument des Johannes Pardeis de Kempnat, Klerikers der Regensburger Diözese: Urkunde über die von Peter Johannes de Capistrano, S. Franziskenordens, zu Nürnberg vom 21. entries.english:
In the name of the Lord, Amen. In the year from His nativity one thousand four hundred fifty-two, in the [?]th indiction, in the sixth year of the pontificate of the most holy father in Christ and our lord, Lord Nicholas, by divine providence Pope Nicholas V, the most religious and devout father Johannes de Capistrano of the Order of St. Francis, on Monday the seventeenth of July, which was the second weekday nearest after the feast of St. Margaret, virgin and martyr, entered the town of Nuremberg, Diocese of Bamberg, and preached there for many days, and in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth [?] and of St. Bernardino performed and worked the signs written below on the days named and in the presence of me, the notary public named below, and of the trustworthy witnesses named below, who were present and standing by.

First, on the day of St. Praxedes, virgin, which was the twenty-first of the said month: Agnes, daughter of Knörlein of Abenberg, Diocese of Eichstätt, a girl of sixteen years, lacking hearing from youth, began to hear well and answered questions directly. Likewise Anna the baker [?], a widow, on the day stated above, who could not walk without crutches for three years, walked alone and put the crutches aside. Likewise Gerdrudis [?], wife of Ulrich Lang, who had not walked for one and a half years without help, now walks well. Likewise Anna, wife of Heinrich Weiss of Lindenbach [?], who could not walk for six years without two crutches, now walks well and upright without any help. Likewise Friedrich Reuscher went with two crutches to the place or market where the sick of the new hospital of the said town were treated and, having left the crutches, went home. Likewise the father of Lord Andreas, vicar of the church of St. Sebald in the said town, Diocese of Bamberg, who had not walked for fourteen weeks without help, walked alone. Likewise Anna, wife of Ulrich Hodler, was carried in a chair to the place of the sick and went her ways without any help. Likewise Konrad Payr of Uttenhofen, Diocese of Eichstätt, who had not walked for three years without crutches or other notable help, was also healed, so that he could walk well alone and without help. Likewise Johannes of Schaunfelt, Diocese of Würzburg, who had not walked for two years nor could take a single step, recently walked without any help. And these things were done on the day stated above. Witnesses of the above: Jodocus Fronhofer and Johannes Scheurer [?], of the Diocese of Bamberg, trustworthy men.

On the day of St. Mary Magdalene, which was the twenty-second of the said month, he performed and worked the signs written below. Likewise Agnes Liderin of Thundorff, Diocese of Eichstätt, who had not seen for eight years except a little, which was white, but nothing distinctly [?], but when touched with the sanctuary saw distinctly [?] many things that were shown to her, and the chapel of the Blessed Virgin and many other things. Witnesses: Jodocus Fronhoffer, Ulrich of Augsburg. Likewise Mostel of Diepersdorf, who had not walked for nine weeks and was carried there, was healed so that he went away alone without help. Witnesses: the provident men Ludwig Pfintzing and Rupert Haller, councillors of the said town. Likewise Sebald, son of Gerlach, in a certain street commonly called Jhergas [?] in the town of Nuremberg, who had not heard for sixteen years, was healed and heard everything that was said to him. Witnesses: the honorable Lord, the provost of Neunkirchen; Jodocus Fronhofer, Diocese of Bamberg. Likewise Friedrich of Pölling, Diocese of Eichstätt, who had not walked for six years, walked well when touched with the sanctuary. Witnesses: Jodocus Fronhoffer, Johannes Zerngibel. Likewise Katherina, daughter of Johannes Türsen of Windischenhenpach, Diocese of Eichstätt, who had not spoken from Pentecost until the day stated above, began to speak these words: "Maria hilff mir ich wil gern frum sein und wil peten und zu kirchen gen" ("Mary, help me, I would gladly be pious and will pray and go to church"), and many other words. Witnesses: the reverend father, the Lord Suffragan of Bamberg; Jodocus Fronhoffer.

On the day of St. Apollinaris, which was the twenty-third of the said month, he performed and worked the signs written below. First, Lord Johannes Scherling, priest of the Diocese of Regensburg, of Dietfurt, who had not seen for ten years, regained his sight so that he recognized colors and many other things distinctly. Witnesses: the provident men Ludwig Pfintzing, Rupert Haller. Likewise Ulrich Payr of Herzogenaurach, Diocese of Würzburg, had a youth of about nine years who had not walked for three years without notable help; he was healed so that he could walk alone and without limping. Witnesses: Ulrich of Augsburg, Johannes Schütz. Likewise Katherina Marckhartin of Aw, Diocese of Würzburg, who had not heard for sixteen [?] years, was healed so that she heard like a healthy person. Witnesses: Ulrich of Augsburg, Johannes Lamber. Likewise Mathens Lang of Bamberg, a man of about fifty years, who had not heard from youth, was healed so that he heard all the weighty words spoken to him; previously he did not hear without great shouting, so that it was necessary to shout into his ears or to signal to him with signs. Witnesses: the provident men Berchtold Pfintzing, Rupert Haller, councillors of the said town.

On the day of St. James, which was the twenty-fifth of the said month, he performed and worked the signs noted below. First, Martin the bathkeeper of Heilsbronn, who had not walked for three years without crutches and sticks, was healed and walked without the aforesaid aids, recently, and limped a little. Witnesses: the provident men Ludwig Pfintzing, Rupert Haller. Likewise Johannes Fistulator, who had not seen distinctly for two years, regained his sight so that he distinguished colors and many other things; asked to tell the truth on his conscience, he said that he saw well. Witnesses: the provident Ludwig Pfintzing, Friedrich Henger. Likewise Agnes Senfftin of Schwabach, Diocese of Eichstätt, who also said on her conscience that she had not heard for seventeen years, was healed so that she hears well what people commonly say [?]. Witnesses: the same, immediately. Likewise Katherina Schupffin of Langenfeld, Diocese of Würzburg, who had not walked for two years without crutches, put them aside and recently walked without help. Witnesses: the same. Likewise Kunegundis of Morstetten, daughter of Johannes Schutz, Diocese of Eichstätt, who had not seen for eight years in one eye and in the second for one year, so that in the last year she was wholly blind, came to the customary place of the sick of the said town and, touched there with the sanctuary, was healed, first in the eye in which she had not seen for eight years, and immediately afterwards in the other, so that she saw colors well, the habit of the devout father and his color, and many other things distinctly. Asked on her conscience, she said that she had not seen in the aforesaid years. Witnesses: the provident men Jodocus Tetzel, Ludwig Pfintzing, councillors of the said town. And all these things were done on the day stated above.

On the day of St. Anne, which was the twenty-sixth of the said month, he performed and worked: first, the wife of Johannes Rieter, a notable citizen of the said town, who had better hearing in one ear, and a certain woman surnamed Schallin, who was healed in one ear. Asked on their consciences, they said that they heard better. Witnesses of these: the honorable men Lord Friedrich Kress, Johannes Ulstatt.

On the day next after St. Anne, which was the twenty-seventh of the said month, he performed and worked: Elizabeth Gleisenbergerin of the Diocese of Bamberg, who had not heard well for three years, was healed so that she hears well. Witnesses: the provident Ludwig Pfintzing, Rupert Haller. Likewise Barbara, daughter of Benigner of Halprun, who had not heard well for twelve years and half, had better hearing, as she affirmed. Likewise the daughter of Hanrich Linthner [?] of the said town, who had not heard in one ear from youth, was healed. Witnesses: the Lord Prior of the Carthusians of Guttenstein, Ludwig Pfintzing. Likewise Margaretha, daughter of Albert [?] Kreutzer of Neustadt, who had not heard well from youth, was healed and hears well. Witnesses: the Lord Prior as above, Johannes Lamber. Likewise Lord Johannes Spigel of the Teutonic Order of Rothenburg, who had not walked for half a year, was healed so that he could cross over without any help. Witnesses: the Lord Prior of Guttenstein and the Lord Procurator of the Carthusians in the said town. Likewise Heinrich of Felkirchen, who could not walk without crutches, was healed so that he walked alone and without help, recently. Witnesses: Brother Ulrich of Heilsbronn, priest, Ludwig Pfintzing. Likewise Johannes Gotz of Amelsdorff, who had not heard well for six years, was healed. Witnesses: Oswald Flock, Friedrich Walther. Likewise Margaretha, daughter of Reuzer [?] of Bamberg, who had not seen in one eye from youth, was healed and saw well; she was a girl of about twelve years and said on her conscience that it was so. Witnesses: Thomas Pibracher, Caspar Grobitz.

On the day of St. Martha, which was [...] day of the said month, he performed and worked: Dorothea Gleisbergerin, nun of Brindlach, Diocese of Bamberg, who could not lift one arm, regained the health of the arm so that she could lift it fully as she wished and with advantage, and she said on her conscience that she was very well, though in other limbs she still suffered infirmities. Witnesses: Lord Friedrich Kress, Johannes Samelhaymer [?]. Likewise Margaretha, daughter of Bartholomäus, tailor of Otting, who had not seen with one eye for eleven years, was healed so that she saw well; and her father, asked in her presence to tell the truth, said on his conscience that it was so, and other men said likewise. Witnesses: Rupert Haller, Johannes Lamber, citizens of the said town. And these things were done on the day stated above.

On the day of the saints Abdon and Sennen, which was the penultimate day of the said month, he performed and worked: the wife of Friedrich Weyschent, who had not heard well in one ear for ten years, was healed. Witnesses: Ludwig Pfintzing, Albert Tanchenstorffer [?]. Likewise Margaretha von der Lunstat, daughter of Horsthen [?], Diocese of Eichstätt, who had not heard for fourteen weeks, was healed and was well, and asked on her conscience whether she told the truth, she said that she was healthy. Witnesses: the valiant men, the knights Heinrich and Johannes, lords of Eglofstein. Likewise Agnes, daughter of Leonhard Husvogel [?], who had not heard well in one ear for three years, was healed and hears well. Witnesses: Heinrich Slosser, Heinrich Smoll. Likewise the wife of Vincent of the town of Dinkelsbühl, who could not walk for fifteen weeks and was carried in a chair, was healed and recently walked without any help. Witnesses: the provident men Rupert Haller, Heinrich Slosser. Likewise Michael Hackenfleschin of Augsburg, who had not heard without great shouting for twelve years, was healed and heard everything that bystanders said in the usual manner; a woman of good standing from the aforesaid city, also asked on her conscience. Witnesses: the lords, the knights of Eglofstein mentioned.

On the last day of the said month he performed and worked: Katherina, wife of the smith of Larbendorff, who could not walk for thirty years without crutches, put the crutches aside and walked and said that she was well, and recently walked. Witnesses: Johannes Oberndorffer [?], Jodocus Fronhoffer. Likewise Margaretha, wife of Heinrich Rudel of Herzogenaurach, Diocese of Würzburg, who had not walked for four years without a stick, put it aside and walked. Witnesses: Ulrich of Augsburg, Johannes Meuthsner [?]. Likewise Anna, wife of Johannes Aman, of Rosenberg, Diocese of Eichstätt, who had not heard well for twenty years, was healed. Witnesses: two brothers of the monastery of St. Giles, of the Order of St. Benedict, in the town of Nuremberg.

On the feast of St. Peter in Chains, which was the first day of August, he performed and worked: Georg Halbmaister, who had not heard in one ear for ten years, was healed. [...] Witnesses: Ulrich of Augsburg, Thomas Pibracher. Likewise Katherina Kuntzin [?], who had not heard in one ear for twenty years, was healed. Witnesses: Rupert Haller, Jodocus Fronhoffer. Likewise Katherina Krawtt [?] [...]bergerin, who had not heard in one ear for twenty years, was healed; and these persons are of the town of Nuremberg and of the Diocese of Bamberg. Witnesses: Rupert Haller, Johannes Lamber. Likewise the daughter of Johannes Keym, who had not heard from youth, was healed and hears well. Witnesses: Johannes Lamber, Johannes Schütz. Likewise Heinrich Han had a youth of about seven years who could not walk except with two crutches, and he was healed so that he walked without any help. Witnesses: Johannes Lamber, Johannes Schütz. Likewise the son of Konrad Ritter, who had not heard from youth, was healed. Witnesses: the same, immediately. Likewise Anna [?] Anne Rosin [?], who could not walk well from youth, walked well and was healed. Witnesses: Johannes Somelhayn, Berchtold Dure.

On the day of St. Sixtus, which was the sixth day of the said month, he performed and worked: Kunigundis of Schlüsselfeld, who could not walk without a stick, put it aside and recently walked. Witnesses: Ludwig Pfintzing, Heinrich Potz. Likewise Alma [?] Schiepranttin of Werd, Diocese of Bamberg, who could not open one hand for twelve weeks, was healed and could open it well. Witnesses: the provident men Nikolaus Gross, Johannes Fronhoffer. Likewise Cristina of St. Katherine of the town of Nuremberg, who had not heard for three years, was healed and hears well. Witnesses: the provident men, councillors of the said town, Nikolaus Gross, Anthonius Tucher. Likewise Felicitas, widow, of Stampuhel, Diocese of Bamberg, who had not heard well for twelve years, was healed. Witnesses: the provident men, councillors Ludwig Pfintzing, Nikolaus Gross. Likewise Konrad Torner of Lemburg, who could not walk without crutches and was carried in a cart, put the crutches aside and went away without any help. Witnesses: the provident men, councillors of the said town, Johannes Volkmair, Nikolaus Gross. Likewise Rudolf Sayler also has better hearing, as he affirmed. Likewise a certain Salnator [?] in the town of Nuremberg, who was carried in a chair to the customary place, could not walk and was healed, and walked to his house without any help. Witnesses: the provident men Ludwig Pfintzing, Anthonius Tucher.

On the day of St. Lawrence, which was the tenth day of the said month, he performed and worked: Heinrich the baker, who had not heard well for half a year, was healed. Witnesses: Ludwig Pfintzing, Jodocus Fronhoffer. Likewise Johannes Faber of Würzburg, who could not walk without crutches, put them aside and walked. Witnesses: the same, immediately. Likewise Andreas Tolz, who had not seen with one eye for twenty years, regained its sight, since earlier he had been a beggar; the second eye is not sound. Witnesses: the same, immediately. Likewise Barbara Tasthennerin, who could not open her right hand nor move her fingers, was healed by touch of the sanctuary so that she could open it well and move her fingers; asked on her conscience whether she told the truth, she said on her conscience that she had not been able to open it for three years nor move her fingers. Witnesses: the illustrious prince Karl of Baden and the valiant knight Rupert of Stauffen. Likewise Anna Plezin [?] of Rotenbach [?] also could not move her hand and was healed. Witnesses: Friedrich of Eglofstein, Thomas Grander. Likewise Margaretha of Rothenburg, Diocese of Würzburg, also has better sight. Likewise Swena also has better hearing, as she says. Likewise Lanng of Werd, who had not walked for fifteen weeks, walks much better.

And all these things were done in great pressure of crowds. In faith and testimony of the truth concerning all and each of the above, I, the notary public named below, was asked and requested on behalf of the provident and circumspect men, the lords consuls and proconsuls of the said town of Nuremberg, Diocese of Bamberg, [?] for the evidence of the above, to draw up one or more public instruments. These things were all done in the year, indiction, pontificate, months and days noted and described above, in the presence of the above-mentioned witnesses and many other trustworthy persons, in faith and testimony of all and each of the above, who were asked and requested.

And I, Johannes Pardeis of Kepnat, cleric of the Diocese of Regensburg, notary by sacred imperial authority, because I was present together with the witnesses noted above at all and each of the above while they were done and carried out as stated, and saw and heard them done, therefore I drew up from it this present public instrument, written faithfully by another, and put it into this public form, and sealed it with my usual and customary sign and name, in faith and testimony of all the above, asked and requested.

facts.content: was designated as of Rosenperg in the Diocese of Eichstätt.
was healed at Nuremberg of poor hearing she had had for twenty years, through the signs worked by Johannes de Capistrano.
